title: Lukas Brandt (Rheinland) - Contoso Euro Bond UCITS Fund, W class
description: EU Zoom call: a head of fund selection reviews the Contoso Euro Bond UCITS Fund, W class for his approval process. The greeting includes a brief GDPR recording-consent exchange; the seller commits to DDQ answers 'next Tuesday' and to arranging a portfolio manager call by the end of the week.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Good morning, Lukas, thanks for joining. Before we start, I would like to record this call for our internal notes, in line with GDPR. Are you comfortable with that?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Good morning, Casey. Yes, that is fine, you have my consent for the recording.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Thank you. How is the weather with you?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Cold and grey, but nothing unusual for November. The Christmas markets are about to open, so at least that is something to look forward to.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Lovely. Shall we get into it? You mentioned in your email that you are looking at euro bond funds.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yes. We are reviewing our euro fixed income exposure, and the Contoso Euro Bond UCITS Fund, W class, is on our shortlist. The W class is the one our custodian platform carries.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Good to hear. What would you like to understand first?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Duration, mainly. With so much uncertainty around the ECB, I want to understand how the fund is positioned on duration and the yield curve.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Understood. The team manages duration actively around the benchmark, so it can move away from the index when their view on euro rates changes. I would rather not quote the current positioning from memory, though.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Of course. And on the credit side, how does the team think about spreads and credit quality? I would like to know how much of the fund sits in investment grade corporates and how much in government bonds.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: It's an investment grade strategy, so the credit exposure comes mostly from corporate bonds alongside euro government bonds. The exact split moves over time, so I wouldn't want to give you a number off the top of my head.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That makes sense. For our approval process, we will need to run the fund through our due diligence questionnaire, the DDQ. Our research committee meets again in December, so I would like to submit everything before that.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That should be fine. Do you send the DDQ over, or do you use a standard template?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We have our own template, and I will send it to you right after this call.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Great, thank you. I'll send you the completed DDQ answers next Tuesday.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Perfect. It would also help to speak with the portfolio manager before the committee meets, to hear how they see euro rates and credit at the moment.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Of course. I'll arrange a call with the portfolio manager and send you a few time slots by the end of the week.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Excellent. Then I think I have what I need for now.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Anything else I can help with today?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, that is everything. Thank you, Casey, this was very helpful.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: My pleasure, Lukas. Enjoy the Christmas markets, and speak soon.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Thank you, you too. Goodbye.

gold.notes: EU market, W class of the UCITS euro bond fund (SYN-000186). The GDPR recording-consent exchange in the greeting is small talk, not a task. Lukas sending his own DDQ template after the call is a customer-side distractor.
